newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: 60,000 Rwandans fleeing rebels, deeper into Zaire.
newsitem.headline: 60,000 Rwandans fleeing rebels, deeper into Zaire.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency on Friday quoted leaders of 60,000 Rwandan refugees as saying they were moving deeper into Zaire to flee advancing rebels, a shift which could put them out of reach of international aid.
It said the mostly ethnic Hutu refugees had reportedly crossed the Zaire River and were massed to the west of Ubundu town.

"The refugee leaders said they wanted to flee from advancing (ethnic Tutsi-led) Alliance forces. They were afraid of the Alliance and wanted to move on," U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) spokesman Fernando del Mundo told Reuters.
Referring to the 60,000, he said: "If the figure is confirmed we are eventually going to lose them because they are moving further inland, west. They will be virtually inaccessible."

A six-member emergency team from the UNHCR was due to arrive in the city of Kisangani on Sunday to resume aid programmes for refugees in Ubundu and elsewhere in eastern Zaire, spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole told a news briefing.

UNHCR operations in the region halted a week ago and its international staff was evacuated when Kisangani fell to rebel forces last Saturday. Rebel leader Laurent Kabila arrived on Friday in the capital of northeastern Zaire.

The rebels have seized more than a fifth of Zaire since launching their revolt in the east last October, and Kabila says his forces will press on to the diamond capital of Mbuji-Mayi and Zaire's second city Lubumbashi.
UNHCR was seeking permission from the rebels to fly over Ubundu to verify how many Rwandan refugees and displaced Zaireans were there. Estimates range from 75,000 to 150,000.
"We are very worried about the situation of refugees in the Ubundu area," she told a briefing earlier in the day.

Reports indicated that a large concentration of refugees have managed to cross the Zaire River into the west of Ubundu town and that 60,000 had gathered at a site called kilometre 82 in the northern outskirts, near a village called Obilo.

"We were told that tens of thousands of refugees are still on the eastern bank of the river waiting to cross over to the other side," she added. These were mainly women and children and those too weak to swim across.

"Thousands of refugees, the strongest among those who have reached the western side of Ubundu, are moving in different directions, farther into the interior where access to them will be practically impossible," O'Toole said.

UNHCR has not yet succeeded in bringing relief supplies to Ubundu. A 12-tonne shipment of blankets, medicine, plastic sheeting and jerry cans was looted a week ago while sitting on a train in Kisangani waiting to be transported, she said.
